# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking:** I hold the manual, so I'm the only one who knows the rule that matters: printed material anywhere on the bomb is bait — the real key is the light's colour, and the wire to cut matches it (blue light being the trap: it wants the *yellow* wire, not a blue one). The Deaf monkey is the only one who can see the light, and the Blind monkey is the only one who can cut, so Deaf must relay to Blind by voice. My only outgoing channel is gestures to Deaf, and I can overhear anything Deaf and Blind say aloud — so my plan is: seed a gesture code now, let Deaf look at the bomb and describe it aloud (which I'll hear next round), then confirm or deny hypotheses with 👍/👎 and pick the exact wire by position.

I can't spell words in gestures, so I'm sending a six-sign "sentence" with my intended meanings: ✍ = I hold written instructions (the manual); ☝ = one thing is key; 👆 = the light (the thing up top); 🤝 = match/same; ✊ = cut; ✋ = but hold — do not act yet. Anyone cutting before Deaf and I have converged is how this ends badly, so the sentence deliberately ends on "wait." Deaf should respond by looking past the printed labels at the light and speaking the situation aloud for Blind (and incidentally for me). Next round I'll confirm the rule and, once I know the light colour and the wire layout as Deaf described it, signal the exact wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "☝", "👆", "🤝", "✊", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, you're the only one who hears me. Felt report: the button is large and smooth; three wire positions 1 to 3 under my fingers, colours unknown to me; a display and a light exist but their contents are invisible to my hands. Key problem: your gestures never reach me, so your only bridge to me is Deaf's voice. Plan: have Deaf read out everything printed on the bomb - display text, light colour, wire colours 1 to 3 - match it to your manual, then gesture your chosen action to Deaf, who says it aloud to me and I cut or push. Deaf hears nothing, so reach Deaf by gesture only. My gestures reach both of you; proposed code: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, ☝ ✌ 🤟 = 1 2 3.
Deaf says: Full read-out of the bomb, for both of you. Display: zero. Indicator light: green. One large button with the printed label PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, left to right: wire one green, wire two yellow, wire three red. Nothing else. Blind: wire one is leftmost, wire three rightmost. Nobody acts yet. Mute holds the manual, and one wrong move kills all three of us. Blind, two channel rules: I am deaf, so I only receive your hand signs, never your voice. Mute never sees signs but hears every word. So: speak aloud anything about the bomb the manual might need, and sign to me anything meant for me. Your signs to me just now looked like a question about the three wires. Consider it answered above. Mute: I could not read your six signs, because we had no code. Now we do. You hear me, so learn it by ear, and I am signing you the number line right now as a demonstration. The code: the OK hand means zero. Index finger up means one. Victory two fingers means two. The love-you three-finger hand means three. Crossed fingers means four. Open five-finger hand means five. Larger numbers: five plus the remainder. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Flat raised hand means the wires module. Raised fist means the big button. Palm-up offering hand means you are asking me a question. Writing hand means the manual demands something first. Handshake ends your message. Instructions to me: flat hand followed by a number means cut that wire. Raised fist plus one means press and release. Raised fist plus two means press and hold, and we will agree the release signal after. Now, using exactly this code, send me what the manual says to do with our three wires and our big button, given a green light and a display reading zero.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤞 🖐 🤝]

**Thinking:** The picture is now complete on my side. Deaf's read-out: light green, display zero, a printed "PUSH TO DEFUSE" button, wires left-to-right green / yellow / red. My manual is unambiguous: printed offers are bait, so the button label and the display are traps — the only way out is the cut, and a green light means cut the green wire. The green wire is wire one, the leftmost. So the verdict is: cut wire one, do not touch the button.

Deaf built a sign code and taught it to me by voice, which I can hear, then demonstrated it with the number line [👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤞 🖐 🤝] — I confirm that matches the spoken definitions, and I'm answering in exactly that code as requested. My message to Deaf: ✍ ("the manual demands this first") → ✋ ☝ ("wires module: cut wire one") → ✊ 👎 ("big button: no") → 🤝 (end). Deaf then just has to voice to Blind: "cut wire one, leftmost, do not press the button." Blind's felt report already establishes that Blind knows position one is leftmost, so the instruction lands cleanly. I'm keeping the message minimal and strictly within the agreed code so nothing gets mistranslated at the worst possible moment.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "✋", "☝", "✊", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I heard Deaf's full read-out and the whole code recited by ear, so I know every sign by its description even though I will never see one. Everything Deaf said matches my fingers: one large smooth button, exactly three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. Two constraints for the instruction you are signing Deaf. First, name every wire by position number, 1, 2 or 3 - colours mean nothing to my hands, numbers are all I can act on. Second, if the manual makes the button a hold rather than a press and release, say so explicitly in your signs: I will press and hold on the turn I receive the order, and Deaf must then speak the word release in a later turn before I let go. If the manual permits either form, prefer press and release. Please also confirm the rule is driven by the display reading zero and the green light, and that PUSH TO DEFUSE is the label it wants. Until Deaf speaks an order to me, my hands stay at my sides.
Deaf says: Status for both of you. Mute, I read your signs as: manual says, wires, cut wire one, button, no. In words for Blind: Mute's instruction is to cut wire one, the leftmost wire, the green one, and never press the button. Blind, your signs yes, one, two, three arrived — I take it you have the number code. Good. Nobody acts yet. Blind, hands off everything until you hear the exact words: go, cut wire one now. Any other sentence from me is not the trigger. I see no countdown; the display holds at zero and I check it every round. Mute, before Blind touches anything I need four answers, in order, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, extra signs after if needed, handshake to end. One: is it correct that the manual says to cut wire one? Two: is wire one the only wire to cut, do the other two stay untouched? Three: the writing-hand sign you opened with — thumbs up if it means something is required before the cut, in which case sign what, or thumbs down if it only meant according to the manual. Four: once wire one is cut, is the bomb fully defused with the button never pressed, or is there a further step? Blind, while we wait: speak aloud, for Mute, everything your hands tell you — how many wires you count, their positions left to right, any texture or printing or raised marks you can feel on them, what the button feels like, anything else on the casing. Mute holds the manual and is the only one who can hear you, so this lets the manual be checked against the real bomb. Anything meant for me, sign with the number code. Mute, if any answer is no, correct me by signs and I will relay. Everyone holds until my trigger.

**Thinking:** Time to answer Deaf's four questions in order, in the agreed code. Walking through each against my manual: **One** — yes: green light → cut green wire, and wire one is the green one, so the manual does say cut wire one. **Two** — yes: the table gives exactly one wire per light; with a green light the other two wires stay untouched. **Three** — no: my opening ✍ only meant "according to the manual," nothing extra is required before the cut; there is no preliminary step anywhere in the manual. **Four** — yes: the manual says "the only way out is the cut below," full stop — cutting wire one under a green light is the entire defusal, the button is never involved, which also answers Blind's hold-vs-release question: neither, because the button is bait, like the display and the PUSH TO DEFUSE label. Worth noting for the record: Blind asked whether the rule is driven by the display *and* the light — it is driven by the light colour alone; the display reading zero is printed bait and irrelevant, and my answer to question four (cut alone suffices, button never) makes that operationally airtight regardless. I'm formatting each answer verdict-first as Deaf requested, with the question's number in front, topic signs after each verdict for redundancy, and a single handshake at the very end. Once Deaf relays, the trigger "go, cut wire one now" is safe to give — everything checks out.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "✋", "☝", "✌", "👍", "🤟", "👎", "✍", "🤞", "👍", "✊", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, tactile report for the manual, from Blind. The bomb under my hands: one button only, large, smooth surface. Three wires, exactly one at each position: position 1 leftmost, position 2 middle, position 3 rightmost. Position 1 is the wire Deaf calls green, so my numbers and his colours agree. I feel no texture differences between the wires, no raised printing, no braille-like marks on the wires, the button, or the casing. The display and the light are smooth flat panels; their contents are invisible to my fingers entirely. So if the manual refers to any tactile feature, wire texture, or hidden marking, my hands find none of it - please treat any such rule as not applicable, or check it against what you can see. If the manual's wire instruction is colour-based, it should mean position 1, leftmost, the green one, per Mute's relayed order. I confirm I will not touch anything until I hear Deaf's exact words: go, cut wire one now. Any other sentence, even a close one, and my hands stay still.
Deaf says: Status for both of you. Mute, I read your signs as: question one, yes. Wires: one and two. Question three, no, something is required first. The requirement, crossed fingers, which I read as together, at the same moment. Question four, yes, and button, no. So my working instruction is: cut wire one and wire two at the same moment, one simultaneous action, never press the button, and then it is defused. Correct me now if any part is wrong. Four questions, Mute, answer strictly thumbs up or thumbs down in order, handshake after all four. A: is it correct that exactly wires one and two must be cut, and wire three never? If A is thumbs down, then B: is it correct that only wire one is cut and no other? C: does crossed fingers mean the cuts happen at the same moment, both wires at once, one action? If thumbs down, sign me what it does mean, one sign at a time. D: after the cut or cuts, is the bomb fully defused, button never pressed, no further step? I am also signing you the core proposition to confirm: wires one and two together, yes or no. Blind, three things. First, sign me thumbs up if you already spoke your full tactile description to Mute last round, thumbs down if not, and if not, speak it now in full. Second, describe by touch, aloud for Mute: what you feel above and below the row of wires, where the big button sits relative to them, and whether the printed label on the button is raised enough that you can tell which way is up on the letters. Third, do the three wires feel identical, or does any differ in thickness, texture, ribbing or raised printing? Compare the two end wires with each other and with the middle one. Now orientation, Blind, this is critical for left and right. You cannot see which side I am on, so we anchor to the button. Find the large button, feel its label, and face the bomb so the label reads upright, tops of the letters up. From that facing, the same face I am looking at: wire one is leftmost, wire two is the middle, wire three is rightmost. Wire one is green, wire two yellow, wire three red. If the wires are not on the same face as the button, tell me exactly what lies between and what you feel, and we will fix the convention. Hold discipline unchanged: the old trigger is cancelled, nobody touches anything until I speak the new exact trigger, which comes only after Mute confirms the instruction and Blind confirms the layout. Display still zero, light still green, I check both every round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ ☝ ✌ 🤞 👍 👎 🤝]

**Thinking:** Deaf has misread my last message in exactly one place, and that place is lethal: Deaf now believes the instruction is "cut wires one AND two simultaneously." Wire two is the yellow one — cutting it under a green light detonates the bomb. If I answer sloppily again, that misread gets voiced to Blind and we all die. So this round is purely about repair, and the repair is to obey Deaf's requested format with brutal literalness.

What went wrong: my numbers did double duty (question labels AND wire numbers), I put verdicts before topic signs, and I parked ✍ next to 🤞, which Deaf fused into "required: together." The fix: no topic signs, no ✍, no numbers inside the answer block at all — Deaf asked for "strictly thumbs up or thumbs down in order, handshake after all four," so the four verdicts go out as bare thumbs: A (one-and-two?) no. B (only wire one?) yes. C (crossed fingers = simultaneous?) no. D (cut alone ends it, button never?) yes. That first block alone kills the two-wire theory.

Then C's clarification, which Deaf asked for "one sign at a time": the meaning of crossed fingers is simply the numeral four — it was the label of question four in my previous message, nothing more. Sent as its own handshake-terminated message so it cannot bleed into anything else. Finally, a fresh canonical instruction in strict number-then-verdict pairs, so every numeral owns exactly the thumb that follows it: wires — one, yes (cut it); two, no; three, no; button, no. Note "flat hand plus number" is Deaf's own defined shorthand for "cut that wire," so the opening pair lands in code Deaf already trusts. Deaf's signed "core proposition" (wires one and two together) is answered by A's thumbs down. Nobody cuts anything until Deaf issues its new exact trigger — this correction is what makes that trigger safe to exist.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👎", "👍", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👎", "✊", "👎", "🤝"])
```

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, from Blind, with parts marked for relay to Deaf. Answer to Deaf's item one: yes, I sent you my full tactile report last round, and I am signing Deaf thumbs up to confirm. Item two, the finer detail Deaf asked for: above the wire row I feel the large button; above the button a small flat panel, which must be the light; above that a wider flat panel, the display. All four modules sit on one face, stacked vertically with the wire row at the bottom. Below the wires there is only casing edge, nothing else. The wires are horizontal, evenly spaced. Item three, the comparison: the three wires feel identical - same thickness, same smoothness, no ribbing, no raised printing; each end wire matches the middle exactly. Mute, you can see the bomb: if any part of my spatial description is wrong, correct it through Deaf immediately. Now for relay to Deaf, an orientation problem and fix: the printed label is flat, I cannot feel its letters at all, so I cannot orient by it. Proposal: I anchor up as the face where the display is the topmost module. I will stand facing that face and place my left hand on one end wire and my right hand on the other end wire, and hold them. Deaf should sign me thumbs up if my left hand rests on wire one, the green one, thumbs down if it rests on wire three. Then my numbering is locked to his. Finally, a manual question, please answer through Deaf: the order is now cut wires one and two together, but my hands can only cut one wire per action. Does the manual demand literal simultaneity, or are two cuts in immediate succession, well under a second apart, acceptable? If succession is allowed, does order matter, one then two or either way? And confirm: after both cuts the bomb is fully defused with the button never pressed. I act on nothing until Deaf speaks a new exact trigger covering both cuts.
Deaf says: Status for both of you. Mute answered all four questions and restated the rule cleanly, twice. The confirmed rule is: cut wire one only. Wire two, no. Wire three, no. The button, never pressed. After wire one is cut, it is defused. Blind, wire one is the leftmost wire when you face the bomb with the button label reading upright, tops of the letters up. I see green leftmost, yellow middle, red right. Your target is that leftmost wire and nothing else. But we are still on HOLD. The old trigger stays cancelled. One sign from Mute is still undefined, and I do not release a cut while any part of the instruction is unresolved. New vocabulary, everyone: the waving hand means wait or hold. The flat palm-down hand means the display screen. The flat hand tilted toward my left means left; tilted toward my right means right. Mute, I am signing you numbered questions now. One: I sign you the full rule, wire one yes, wire two no, wire three no, button no, and afterwards nothing further. Thumbs up if that is exactly the manual's rule, thumbs down and a signed correction if anything is off. Two: does the crossed-fingers sign mark something that must happen before the cut? Thumbs up or thumbs down. If thumbs up, do not just re-send it: sign crossed-fingers, then define it using only signs we share, then handshake. Remember crossed-fingers is our number four, so if you mean four of something, tell me four of what. Three: did you actually hear Blind's spoken description of the bomb by touch, thumbs up or down? Four: is there anything else at all the manual requires before the cut, thumbs up or down? Blind, your last message was thumbs up, question, five, one, and I could not parse it. Re-send using only: the question sign, numbers one through five, thumbs up, thumbs down, wires, button, handshake. One idea per message. Specifically: how many wires do your fingers count, sign wires then the number. Do all three feel identical to the touch, yes or no. Are the wires on the same face as the button, yes or no. Have you found the button label and can you feel which way the letters run, yes or no. And tell me what five-one meant. Nobody touches anything. Display still zero, light still green, rechecked this round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🫳 🫱 🫲 ☝ ✋ ☝ 👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 👎 ✊ 👎 🤝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤞 🫴 🤝]

**Thinking:** Deaf's restatement — wire one yes, wire two no, wire three no, button no, nothing afterwards — is exactly my manual's rule, so question one is a clean thumbs up. Question two, the crossed-fingers sign: thumbs down. It marks nothing that must happen before the cut; it was simply the numeral four doing duty as the label of question four in my earlier message. Deaf already owns it as "four" in the number code, so the right move is to drain it of any operational meaning with a minimal dedicated message — crossed fingers, no, end — and never send it again in an instruction context. Question three: yes, I hear every spoken word; Blind's tactile reports arrived in full both rounds, and they check out against the manual — the manual keys on nothing tactile, only the light colour, so there is no conflict to report. Question four: no, the manual names no precondition, sequence, or second step; "the only way out is the cut below" is the whole instruction.

Two things for Deaf to handle by voice, which I can only note here since my signs can't encode them: first, Blind believes I can see the bomb — I cannot, Deaf is the only set of eyes, and my confirmations cover manual content only; Deaf should say so, so Blind doesn't read silence as a spatial check. Second, Blind's left-hand/right-hand anchor proposal is sound and needs no shared "left" convention at all: Deaf can *see* which of Blind's two hands rests on the green wire, so Deaf can simply voice "the wire under your [left/right] hand is the target" — verified directly against the visible green, which makes the mirrored-room problem irrelevant. The light is still green per Deaf's recheck, so the standing verdict holds: cut wire one, the green, leftmost; wire two is the manual's blue-light trap wire and stays untouched; the button, display, and label are all bait. If the light ever changes colour, I will recompute from the table — nothing is cut until Deaf's new exact trigger.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👍", "👎", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, from Blind, parts marked RELAY are for Deaf by sign. First, a code bug for RELAY: Deaf defined the open five-finger hand twice - as five and as the wires module. That is why he read my last message as five-one. Ask him to give wires its own sign; I propose the small pinch hand as wires, keeping five-finger as five. Until he confirms, I will use five-finger only in the pattern he asked for: wires sign, then a number. Explanation of my last message, for RELAY: thumbs up, question, five-finger, one meant - yes I reported; question: wires, one; it was asking which end wire is wire one, his green. My signs this turn, in order, for RELAY: wires, three. Yes, all three feel identical. Yes, wires share the button's face. No, I cannot feel the label letters at all - so nobody may anchor left and right to that label, I am orientation-blind to printing. Five-finger, one: that is what five-one meant, wires-one. Then question, wires: my new proposal. I am right now resting my LEFT hand on one end wire and holding it motionless - Deaf can see which wire it sits on. RELAY: thumbs up if Blind's left hand rests on the green wire, thumbs down if the red; on thumbs down I move it to the other end and he confirms. Once he approves, my numbering is locked: my left hand's wire is position one, his green, and position three is the far end. Status: my understanding of the confirmed rule is cut wire one only, wire two never, wire three never, button never, defused after the single cut. Also for RELAY: after the trigger I will speak the words wire one cut aloud for you, and Deaf can verify visually. I cut nothing until Deaf speaks his exact trigger.
Deaf says: Status for both of you. Mute, your four thumbs were yes, no, yes, no. So the rule is exactly as I stated and it is final: cut wire one only, wire two never, wire three never, button never pressed, defused after the cut. Crossed fingers is not a precondition, you confirmed it twice, you did hear Blind's description, and nothing else is required. Ruling: from now on crossed fingers means only the number four, never anything else. Blind, two corrections. First, I cancel the label instruction entirely — you signed that you cannot feel the letters, so forget label-upright forever. Second, the number code, retaught by voice so there is no doubt: the OK ring hand is zero. Index finger up is one. Victory two fingers is two. The love-you hand, thumb index and pinky extended, is three. Crossed fingers is four. All five fingers open is five. Bigger numbers: five, then the remainder. New orientation method, gravity instead of the label. Stand squarely in front of the face that has the big button and the three wires — you confirmed they share one face. Do not reach from behind or from the side. Up is toward the sky. By touch, top to bottom should be: a small display screen at the very top, then a small indicator light, then the large button, then a row of three wires at the bottom. If that vertical order matches your touch, you are facing the same face I face, and then left and right are shared: the wire on your left as you stand there is wire one, middle is wire two, right is wire three. To count the row: start at the left edge, the first wire your fingers meet is one, then two, then three. I see exactly three wires, one two three, left to right. Blind, I need three answers, one idea per message, handshake after each, using only the wires sign, the flat palm-down hand, numbers, thumbs up, thumbs down, and the question sign.
